name: Nginx
description: Static web server. Serves the files in ./html on port 8080.

name: PostgreSQL
description: PostgreSQL 16 database with a named volume. Not published on the host; reach it from other containers on the same network.

name: Redis
description: Redis 7 with append-only persistence. Not published on the host.

name: MariaDB
description: MariaDB 11 database with a named volume and an initial database. Not published on the host.

name: WordPress
description: WordPress with its own MariaDB database. Open port 8081 after the first deploy to finish the setup.

env.description: Password of the WordPress database user

name: Uptime Kuma
description: Self-hosted uptime monitoring with a status page. Open port 3001 after the first deploy.

name: Adminer
description: Lightweight web UI for SQL databases. Open port 8082 and connect to your database from there.

name: Vaultwarden
description: Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible password manager. Open port 8083 after the first deploy. Browsers need HTTPS for the web vault, so put it behind a domain.

env.description: Token for the /admin page. Use an Argon2 PHC hash or a long random string.

name: Gitea
description: Self-hosted Git service with a web UI. Open port 3000 after the first deploy to finish the setup. SSH is not published.

name: Grafana
description: Dashboards and alerting for metrics and logs. Open port 3100 after the first deploy and log in as admin with the password you set.

env.description: Password of the initial admin user

name: Jellyfin
description: Media server for movies, shows and music. Open port 8096 after the first deploy. No media folder is mounted; add a bind mount for your library in the wizard.

name: Home Assistant
description: Home automation hub. Open port 8123 after the first deploy. Runs on bridge networking, so device discovery that needs the host network does not work.

name: Nextcloud
description: Self-hosted file sync and sharing. Open port 8084 after the first deploy. Set the trusted domains to the names you open it with, or Nextcloud refuses them.

env.description: Password of the initial admin user (username admin)
Space-separated host names or IPs you open Nextcloud with, e.g. 192.168.1.10 cloud.example.com

name: Pi-hole
description: Network-wide ad blocker and DNS server. Open port 8085 and sign in at /admin with the generated password, then point your devices or router at this host as DNS server. Port 53 must be free on the host.

env.description: Password of the admin web interface

name: Nginx Proxy Manager
description: Reverse proxy with a web UI and Let's Encrypt certificates. Open port 8086 after the first deploy and sign in with admin@example.com / changeme, then change both. Proxied traffic arrives on ports 8088 (HTTP) and 8443 (HTTPS).

name: Homepage
description: Customizable start page for your services. Open port 3002 after the first deploy and edit the YAML files in the config volume to add your services.

name: File Browser
description: Web file manager for a storage volume. Open port 8089 after the first deploy and sign in with admin / admin, then change the password right away.

name: Syncthing
description: Continuous peer-to-peer file synchronization. Open port 8384 after the first deploy and set a GUI password under Actions, Settings. Sync traffic uses port 22000, local discovery 21027.

name: MySQL
description: MySQL 8.4 database with a named volume and an initial database. Connect to host port 3307 with the root user and the generated root password.

name: MongoDB
description: MongoDB 7 document database with authentication. Connect to host port 27018 with the admin user and the generated password.

name: RabbitMQ
description: Message broker with the management UI. Open port 15673 after the first deploy and sign in with the user and password below. Applications connect over AMQP on port 5673.

name: MinIO
description: S3-compatible object storage. Open the console on port 9101 after the first deploy and sign in with the user and password below. The S3 API listens on port 9100.

name: InfluxDB
description: Time series database, version 2. Open port 8087 after the first deploy and sign in with the user and password below. The API token below is for clients.

name: Ghost
description: Publishing platform and blog with its own MySQL database. Open port 2368 after the first deploy; the admin setup is at /ghost.

env.description: Public URL of the site (change it when you put a domain in front)
Password of the Ghost database user

name: n8n
description: Workflow automation. Open port 5678 after the first deploy and create the owner account.

env.description: Key that encrypts stored credentials; keep it, losing it makes saved credentials unreadable
Time zone for schedules (for example Europe/Berlin)

name: Paperless-ngx
description: Document management with OCR, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis. Open port 8010 after the first deploy and sign in with the admin user below. Drop files into the consume volume to import them.

env.description: Name of the first admin user
Password of the first admin user
Password of the PostgreSQL database user

name: BookStack
description: Wiki and documentation platform with its own MariaDB database. Open port 6875 after the first deploy and sign in as admin@admin.com with the password 'password', then change both.

env.description: Public URL of the wiki (change it when you put a domain in front)
Password of the BookStack database user

name: Linkding
description: Bookmark manager. Open port 9090 after the first deploy and sign in with the admin user below.

name: Plex
description: Media server for movies, shows and music. Open port 32400/web after the first deploy. To claim the server, set PLEX_CLAIM (token from plex.tv/claim, valid 4 minutes) in the wizard, or finish setup from a browser on the same network as the host. Host networking is not available here, so local network discovery (GDM, DLNA) is limited; add the server by IP in your Plex apps. Media uses a named volume; replace it with a bind mount for an existing library.

name: Sonarr
description: TV show manager that finds, downloads and organizes episodes. Open port 8989 after the first deploy. Config and media use named volumes; to use an existing library, replace the media volume with a bind mount in the wizard.

env.description: User ID the app runs as
Group ID the app runs as

name: Radarr
description: Movie manager that finds, downloads and organizes films. Open port 7878 after the first deploy. Config and media use named volumes; to use an existing library, replace the media volume with a bind mount in the wizard.

env.description: User ID the app runs as
Group ID the app runs as

name: Navidrome
description: Music streaming server compatible with Subsonic apps. Open port 4533 after the first deploy and create the admin user on first visit. Music uses a named volume; replace it with a bind mount for an existing library.

name: Audiobookshelf
description: Audiobook and podcast server. Open port 13378 after the first deploy and create the root user on first visit. Libraries use named volumes; replace them with bind mounts for existing files.
